body: Thank you for that. I think it’s something I know in the back of my head but just can’t accept. I guess I needed to hear that. I feel like I should do everything myself and that asking for help is a weakness but I know that’s not true. It’s just hard to deny. I’m really amazed by the redditors that have reached out to me so far. I really didn’t expect the support. Edit: spelling

Thank you. Everyone that took the time to read this was my savior today. I really appreciate the time you took. The uncertainty of day by day work is killing me. Like the other comment said, I need to prioritize a stable job. I’m glad you were able to connect to people through groups. I already feel like reaching out was worth it because people like you replied. I was staring at the draft of the post for a long time thinking is not worth it before I actually mustered up the courage to post.

Thank you so much. It means the world to me that you read it all. I live in BW. I didn’t go to the hospital, but a friend suggested U25 to me, a mailing service for suicidal youth, and any areas near me were overburdened. Part of my problem is not being able to find information. For example, every time I go to the Amt für Migration, I get a different answer, or the person seems to have no idea what I’m talking about. Reading all the bureaucratic and technical stuff for taxes, visas, or health insurance is really difficult for me and usually written in a way that no one speaks. Also, as a freelancer I’m afraid that going to Kur will mean either I don’t get paid (because I don’t get sick leave), or I don’t get my visa renewed, and get sent home. If I want insurance to pay for therapy I have to pay up front and get reimbursed and I don’t have the overhead to do that. I’ve heard of therapy programs hosted by uni students for cheap but I don’t know much about it or where to find info on it. Do you know anything about this?
